correctness.rationale: With unnormalized g(t)=e^(−πt²) and lattice (m,n)∈Z², the unitary Zak transform maps each g_{m,n} to character E_{m,n}Zg. After deleting origin, the unique dual of a remaining atom has Zak quotient [E_{m,n}−(−1)^(m+n)]/conjugate(Zg); numerator cancels at unique Gaussian Zak zero p=(1/2,1/2). Normalize source theta derivative for unscaled g: Zg(p+(u,v))=−κ(u+iv)+O(r²), κ=πθ1'(0,e^(−π))>0. Therefore reciprocal |Zg|² differs from (κ²r²)^(−1) by O(1/r), integrable in 2D uniformly under bounded character numerator. Polar angular averaging of |exp(2π i(nu−mv))−1|²/r² gives 4π/κ² ∫_0^(2πρR) [1−J0(t)]dt/t. Small-t J0=1+O(t²) and large-t |J0(t)|=O(t^(−1/2)) establish log R+O(1) uniformly in lattice direction. Hence coefficient 4/(π|θ1'|²)≈1.54852449; integer time-frequency covariance transfers to every deleted atom. Numerical midpoint quadrature only checks the scale, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Proves Zikkos 2026 Conjecture 4.1 about the squared norms of the unique Gaussian critical-density missing-atom biorthogonals, with a sharp, direction-independent leading coefficient and universal additive error. This is a natural infinite-system stability invariant and makes a sufficient lower-semi-frame summability condition explicit; no necessary complete weight classification is claimed.

limitations: Critical square lattice, unnormalized Gaussian and one deleted atom only.
